premise: After my husband died, I emptied my $75,000 401(k) to help my sister-in-law purchase a historic bed-and-breakfast, signing a promissory note for repayment plus 20% equity in the B&B; she then sold the B&B to a hotel chain for $1.4 million, forged a document stating the note was a gift, and left me with nothing. I traced the sale, proved the forgery through handwriting analysis, and the court ordered her to pay me $310,000 in restitution — she couldn’t, so I placed a lien on her inherited lake home and eventually took possession; now I run that home as a vacation rental called ‘Promissory Lakehouse,’ with every booking confirmation email detailing the fraud case and her name listed as the ‘Involuntary Patron.’
